question.worked_solution:
We convert the absolute value inequality into a compound inequality to remove the absolute value. 

The inequality specifies every number $3-2x$ whose distance from zero is greater than $3.$ This corresponds to the following compound inequality:

$$
\begin{aligned}3-2x & <-3 & \text{or} &  & 3-2x & >3\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can solve each inequality using the usual methods. (Remember that whenever we multiply or divide by a negative number, we have to flip the inequality signs.)

$$
\begin{aligned}3-2x & <-3 &  &  & 3-2x & >3 \\ -2x & <-6 &  &  & -2x & >0 \\ x & >3 &  &  & x & <0\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the final solution is

$$
\begin{aligned}x & <0 & \text{or} &  & x & >3.\end{aligned}
$$
